name: DataScript
tagline: Immutable in-memory database with Datomic-style Datalog queries for Clojure, ClojureScript and JavaScript.
description: DataScript, by Nikita Prokopov (tonsky), is an immutable in-memory database and Datalog query engine that brings Datomic's data model to the browser and the JVM. Data is stored as entity-attribute-value datoms in sorted indexes, every transaction returns a new database value instead of mutating state, and you query with Datalog, the pull API or entity navigation. That makes it a natural single source of truth for front-end application state: views can query it reactively and old values are cheap to keep for undo. Since version 1.5 it can also persist to pluggable durable storage on the JVM. It is actively maintained (1.8.1, August 2026) and underpins tools such as Roam Research, Logseq and Athens.

scale.notes: Whole database lives in memory of one process; optional JVM storage persists and lazily loads index segments.

strengths: Datomic-compatible data model and Datalog queries in the browser
Immutable database values make undo, diffing and reactive views simple
Pull API and entity navigation for tree-shaped reads
Small, dependency-light library with long-term active maintenance
weaknesses: Entire database must fit in memory
No built-in history or as-of queries like Datomic
Durable storage only on the JVM, not in JavaScript
Datalog performance degrades on very large datasets
useCases: Client-side application state for ClojureScript apps
In-memory graph queries over modest datasets
